title: Coordinating EV charging modes and energy system planning reveals uneven savings across Europe - Nature Energy
gist: A Nature Energy research briefing (paywalled beyond the abstract) reports that when charging-infrastructure capital costs are built into a European energy-system model, unidirectional smart charging (V1G) cuts annual system costs by up to 4.5%, while bidirectional charging (V2G) earns its money through market revenues concentrated in solar-dominated systems. The stated policy implication is that uniform EU charging-infrastructure targets are mismatched to heterogeneous national energy systems.

insights.claim: Unidirectional smart charging (V1G) delivers up to 4.5% in annual energy-system cost savings in a European model that internalizes charging-infrastructure costs.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Caps the plausible system-level savings pitch for smart-charging software and managed-charging utilities: a few percent of system cost, not a step change.
insights.quote: unidirectional smart charging delivers up to 4.5% in annual system cost savings
insights.locator: Including the costs of charging infrastructure

insights.claim: Bidirectional (V2G) charging monetizes primarily through market revenues rather than through system-cost reduction, and those revenues are substantial specifically in solar-dominated power systems.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: V2G business cases should be underwritten in high-solar markets (Iberia, Italy, Greece) where daily price spreads exist, not modelled as a uniform European revenue stream.
insights.quote: bidirectional charging technology generates substantial market revenues in solar-dominated systems
insights.locator: Including the costs of charging infrastructure

insights.claim: The savings from coordinated EV charging are explicitly uneven across European countries rather than uniform, so national generation mix is the variable that determines charging-mode value.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Country selection, not technology selection, is the dominant driver of returns for V2G hardware and aggregator businesses in Europe.
insights.locator: Coordinating EV charging modes and energy system planning

themes.theme: Uniform EU targets vs national heterogeneity

insights.claim: EU Regulation 2023/1804 (AFIR) imposes mandatory, uniform public EV charging capacity requirements across member states, a design the briefing implicitly criticizes by arguing targets should be differentiated by national energy system.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Signals possible future revision or differentiation of AFIR deployment mandates; charge-point operators building to uniform targets may be over- or under-building relative to where value actually accrues.
insights.quote: This regulation sets mandatory EU targets for the deployment of alternative-fuel infrastructure, including uniform public EV charging capacity requirements.

insights.claim: The recommended policy unit is the national energy system rather than the EU-wide average, implying charging-infrastructure targets should be set country by country.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Watch for member-state-level deviation in charging mandates as a policy catalyst for regional charge-point and V2G suppliers.
insights.quote: Thus, charging infrastructure targets should account for differences across diverse national energy systems.

insights.claim: Co-optimizing charging-infrastructure deployment together with energy-system planning — rather than treating chargers as an exogenous cost — is presented as the analytical advance that produces cost-optimal V1G/V2G deployment maps for Europe.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A reusable lens: any storage-like asset's system value should be netted against its own capex inside the model, which typically deflates headline flexibility-value claims.
insights.quote: Fig. 1: Cost-optimal EV charging infrastructure deployment in Europe.

insights.claim: Prior European work found that infrastructure costs and utilization rates dominate the levelized cost of EV charging, framing charger utilization as the key economic variable rather than electricity price alone.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Charge-point operator equity stories hinge on utilization curves; under-utilized public networks are structurally uneconomic regardless of power prices.
insights.quote: highlighting the effect of infrastructure costs and utilization rates on total charging costs
insights.locator: Lanz, L., Noll, B., Schmidt, T. S. & Steffen, B.
